2027-01-22.title: Third Friday of Denha · Commemoration of the Evangelists
2027-01-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Signs and wonders through the apostles
In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel
2027-01-22.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-22.verse: For though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
theo: On the third Friday of Denha the Church honours the four Evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, through whom the good news has reached every land. The readings show what the Gospel is: God making himself known. On Mount Carmel Elijah repairs the broken altar with twelve stones, “according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob”, soaks the offering with water and prays: “Answer me, O LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that you, O LORD, are God, and that you have turned their hearts back.” Fire falls, and the whole people cries: “The LORD indeed is God; the LORD indeed is God.” This is Denha: the true God revealed. In Acts the same God works “many signs and wonders” through the apostles, and the sick are laid in the streets so “that Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them”.

In the Gospel Jesus calls the Twelve by name; among them are “James son of Zebedee, and his brother John” and “Thomas and Matthew the tax collector”. He sends them out: “As you go, proclaim the good news, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’” And he adds: “You received without payment; give without payment.” The Evangelists did in writing what the Twelve did by voice: Matthew and John from among the Twelve, Mark and Luke from the circle of Peter and Paul. Paul tells the Corinthians what it cost: “We are fools for the sake of Christ”, hungry, homeless, reviled; yet “in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.” Through their four books the Evangelists are fathers in faith to us too. In Kerala the faith first preached by the Apostle Thomas has been fed for centuries by these Gospels, read at every Holy Qurbana.

2027-01-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, you sent the Twelve to proclaim that the kingdom of heaven has come near, and through the four Evangelists your Gospel has reached us. Let the fire of your Spirit fall on our hearts, so that we may say with all your people: the Lord indeed is God. Make us glad to give freely what we have freely received. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Gospel book is carried in honour and Christ speaks when it is read. Then the Holy Spirit is invoked on the offerings: the fire Elijah prayed for comes upon our altar.

family.explain: Jesus chose twelve friends and sent them to tell everyone that God's kingdom is near. Matthew and John were among them, and later they wrote down the Good News for us. Mark and Luke wrote Gospels too.

illus: A retired schoolteacher in Idukki has given away more than five hundred copies of the Gospel of Luke in Malayalam, one at a time, to bus conductors, nurses and neighbours. Asked why, she said: someone gave me the Gospel for nothing when I was a girl. I received without payment; I give without payment.

homily: Dear friends, on the third Friday of Denha we honour the four Evangelists. The first reading takes us to Mount Carmel. Elijah rebuilds the broken altar of the LORD with twelve stones, pours water on the offering three times, and prays: answer me, O LORD, so that this people may know that you are God. The fire falls, and the people cry: the LORD indeed is God (1 Kings 18:39).

Denha means manifestation: God showing himself. In Acts he shows himself again: many signs and wonders are done through the apostles, and people lay the sick in the streets hoping Peter's shadow will fall on them (Acts 5:12–15).

In the Gospel Jesus calls the Twelve by name and sends them: as you go, proclaim the good news, the kingdom of heaven has come near. You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:7–8). Matthew and John were among them. Mark and Luke learned from Peter and Paul. What the apostles preached, the Evangelists wrote, so that the good news could reach us.

It was not easy. Paul says: we are fools for the sake of Christ, hungry, poorly clothed, homeless. But he also says: in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel (1 Corinthians 4:15). Each time we open a Gospel, these fathers in faith speak to us. Let us read one Gospel this month, and pass on freely what we have freely received. Amen.
kids: Children, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote down the story of Jesus for us! Jesus said: you received for free, so give for free. Share something with a friend today, and read a little of the Gospel every day.

intro: Theme: “In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.”
The four Evangelists: God revealed, the Twelve sent, fathers in faith.

q: When all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and said, “The LORD indeed is God; the LORD indeed is God.”
But these are written so that you may come to believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that through believing you may have life in his name.
points.apply: Thank God for the Gospels and those who brought them to Kerala.

q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
As you go, proclaim the good news, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’ Cure the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
points.apply: Share the Gospel freely with one person this week.

q: Your words were found, and I ate them, and your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart; for I am called by your name, O LORD, God of hosts.
For though you might have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers. Indeed, in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
points.apply: Read one Gospel chapter every day.

concl: The Evangelists wrote what the apostles preached.
Through the Gospel they are our fathers in faith; we must pass it on.
